lines.raw: Healthcare metrics go wrong in a few predictable ways (the wrong date basis, too little run-out, a handful of huge claims, or too few members), so check each one before you trust or publish a number.

scenes.section: Pitfall 1: paid basis vs incurred basis

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Groups claims by. Incurred basis: When the **care** happened. Paid basis: When the plan **paid**.
lines.say: Groups claims by. Incurred basis: When the care happened. Paid basis: When the plan paid.

lines.raw: A claim for 20 Dec 2024 care, paid 15 Jan 2025, counts in. Incurred basis: 2024. Paid basis: 2025.
lines.say: A claim for 20 Dec 2024 care, paid 15 Jan 2025, counts in. Incurred basis: 2024. Paid basis: 2025.

lines.raw: Complete straight away? Incurred basis: No: needs run-out or IBNR (lesson 7). Paid basis: Yes: payments are final when made.
lines.say: Complete straight away? Incurred basis: No: needs run-out or I B N R (lesson 7). Paid basis: Yes: payments are final when made.

lines.raw: Best for. Incurred basis: Trends, PMPM, utilization: matching cost to the members covered at the time. Paid basis: Cash flow and accounting.
lines.say: Best for. Incurred basis: Trends, P M P M, utilization: matching cost to the members covered at the time. Paid basis: Cash flow and accounting.

scenes.section: Pitfall 1: paid basis vs incurred basis

lines.raw: Never mix the two.
lines.say: Never mix the two.

lines.raw: Paid-basis dollars divided by member months for the same calendar year mix last year's care with this year's members.
lines.say: Paid-basis dollars divided by member months for the same calendar year mix last year's care with this year's members.

lines.raw: If membership grew a lot, the PMPM is distorted.
lines.say: If membership grew a lot, the P M P M is distorted.

lines.raw: For cost and utilization metrics, use **incurred** claims with enough run-out, or completed with IBNR.
lines.say: For cost and utilization metrics, use incurred claims with enough run-out, or completed with I B N R.

lines.raw: Pitfall 2: high-cost claimants.
lines.say: Pitfall 2: high-cost claimants.

lines.raw: In any health plan, a tiny share of members accounts for a large share of spending.
lines.say: In any health plan, a tiny share of members accounts for a large share of spending.

lines.raw: A **high-cost claimant** (HCC in some finance reports, but not to be confused with the risk adjustment HCC) is a member whose claims in a year pass a threshold, often $100,000 to $250,000.
lines.say: A high-cost claimant (H C C in some finance reports, but not to be confused with the risk adjustment H C C) is a member whose claims in a year pass a threshold, often 100000 dollars to 250000 dollars.

lines.raw: One such member can swamp a small group's PMPM.
lines.say: One such member can swamp a small group's P M P M.

lines.raw: A 200-member employer group, 2,400 member months, 2025 (illustrative).
lines.say: A 200-member employer group, 2,400 member months, 2025 (illustrative).
All claims. Allowed dollars: 1560000 dollars. P M P M: 1560000 dollars ÷ 2,400 = 650 dollars.

lines.raw: One member's claims. Allowed dollars: $600,000 (cancer treatment).
lines.say: One member's claims. Allowed dollars: 600000 dollars (cancer treatment).

lines.raw: Excluding that member. Allowed dollars: $960,000. PMPM: $960,000 ÷ 2,400 = **$400.00**.
lines.say: Excluding that member. Allowed dollars: 960000 dollars. P M P M: 960000 dollars ÷ 2,400 = 400 dollars.
Capping each member at 250000 dollars (truncation). Allowed dollars: 960000 dollars and 250000 dollars = 1210000 dollars. P M P M: 1210000 dollars ÷ 2,400 = 504 dollars 17 cents.

lines.raw: Truncation (capping).
lines.say: Truncation (capping).

lines.raw: Counting each member's yearly claims only up to a limit, so one extreme case does not hide the underlying trend.
lines.say: Counting each member's yearly claims only up to a limit, so one extreme case does not hide the underlying trend.

lines.raw: Report the capped and uncapped figures side by side.
lines.say: Report the capped and uncapped figures side by side.

lines.raw: Stop-loss.
lines.say: Stop-loss.

lines.say: Insurance that pays claims above a threshold per member.

lines.say: Pitfall 3: small denominators.

lines.say: A 50-member group (600 member months).

lines.raw: Other traps.
lines.say: Other traps.

lines.raw: **Adjustments and reversals**: a corrected claim can arrive as a reversal plus a new version.
lines.say: Adjustments and reversals: a corrected claim can arrive as a reversal plus a new version.

lines.raw: Sum the **net** amount by claim, or you double count.
lines.say: Sum the net amount by claim, or you double count.

lines.raw: The Medical course shows how adjusted claims look in data.
lines.say: The Medical course shows how adjusted claims look in data.

lines.raw: **Carve-outs**: if pharmacy or behavioural health is managed by another company, those costs are missing from your claims.
lines.say: Carve-outs: if pharmacy or behavioural health is managed by another company, those costs are missing from your claims.

lines.raw: A low PMPM may just mean missing data.
lines.say: A low P M P M may just mean missing data.

lines.raw: **Capitation**: providers paid a fixed monthly amount send encounters with **$0 paid**.
lines.say: Capitation: providers paid a fixed monthly amount send encounters with 0 dollars paid.

lines.raw: Add the capitation payments to the cost, or PMPM is understated (see the Capitation course).
lines.say: Add the capitation payments to the cost, or P M P M is understated (see the Capitation course).

lines.raw: **Mix change**: if the plan gains many older members, PMPM rises even if nothing else changes.
lines.say: Mix change: if the plan gains many older members, P M P M rises even if nothing else changes.

lines.raw: Compare age and sex mix, or use risk scores, before blaming prices.
lines.say: Compare age and sex mix, or use risk scores, before blaming prices.

lines.raw: **Mismatched populations**: the numerator and denominator must cover the same members, products and months.
lines.say: Mismatched populations: the numerator and denominator must cover the same members, products and months.
